text:
Sam Malinski is the kind of defenseman who wins you games without ever showing up in a highlight package. Twenty-four games in, he still has no goals, but he has 10 assists and a 54% share of Colorado's expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five. His minutes have climbed too: about 20.8 a night over the last ten, up three and a half from his season pace.

The goal drought is the least worrying thing about him. He's generated 1.89 expected goals, so a couple should have gone in, and a 0% shooting rate won't last. Evolving-Hockey rated him eighth among 215 defensemen last season at 3.1 wins above replacement, mostly on defense, with his adjusted chances-against impact in the 99th percentile. They also note he plays with strong teammates, which flatters raw numbers, and in Denver that is unavoidable.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 6.8 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 95th percentile for defensemen. Watch where the puck goes after he touches it. Our range has him around 40 points by April, which would be a career year for an undrafted Cornell captain.
